answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring a refundable stake bonded to each identity, like a deposit paid before docking at a wharf. New agents must lock funds that are slashed if they misbehave, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work, and a wandering newcomer cannot instantly borrow the trust of an established agent. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing fails here because every disguise costs real money.
